audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet siege-release oracle, four excluded men, abandoned Aramean camp, public announcement, and gate-officer death narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for impossible-price oracle, skeptical officer, four men with skin disease at the gate, hunger-risk decision, panic in Aramean camp, abandoned wealth and food, concealment then disclosure, cautious reconnaissance, famine relief, crowd crush, and fulfilled warning.

verses.restored: Elisha said, Hear word of YHWH: Thus says YHWH, About this time tomorrow a seah of fine flour shall be for one shekel and two seahs of barley for one shekel at gate of Samaria.

The officer on whose hand king leaned answered man of Divine and said, Look, if YHWH made windows in heavens, could this thing be? He said, Look, you shall see it with your eyes, but from there you shall not eat.
Four men afflicted with skin disease were at entrance of gate. They said each to his neighbor, Why are we sitting here until we die?

If we say, Let us enter city, famine is in city and we shall die there. If we sit here, we shall die. Now therefore come, let us fall to camp of Arameans. If they preserve us alive, we shall live; and if they put us to death, we shall die.
They rose in twilight to enter camp of Arameans. They came to edge of camp of Aram, and look, no man was there.

For Lord had caused camp of Aram to hear sound of chariots, sound of horses, sound of a great force. They said each to his brother, Look, king of Israel hired against us kings of Hittites and kings of Egypt to come upon us.
They rose and fled in twilight, abandoned tents, horses, and donkeys—the camp as it was—and fled for their lives.

Those afflicted with skin disease came to edge of camp, entered one tent, ate and drank, carried from there silver, gold, and garments, went and hid them; they returned, entered another tent, carried from there, went and hid.

They said each to his neighbor, We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until morning light, guilt will find us. Now therefore come, let us go and tell house of king.
They came and called to gatekeepers of city and told them, saying, We came to camp of Aram, and look, no man there, no human voice, only horses bound, donkeys bound, and tents as they were.
Gatekeepers called, and they told it inside house of king.

King arose in night and said to his servants, Let me tell you now what Arameans did to us. They know we are hungry, so they went out from camp to hide in field, saying, When they come out from city, we will seize them alive and enter city.

One of his servants answered and said, Please let men take five of remaining horses that remain in city—look, they are like all multitude of Israel that remains in it, or like all multitude of Israel that has come to an end—and let us send and see.
They took two chariot teams with horses, and king sent after camp of Aram, saying, Go and see.
They went after them as far as Jordan, and look, all way was full of garments and vessels Arameans threw away in their haste. Messengers returned and told king.
People went out and plundered camp of Aram. A seah of fine flour was for one shekel and two seahs of barley for one shekel, according to word of YHWH.
King appointed officer on whose hand he leaned over gate, and people trampled him in gate, and he died, as man of Divine spoke when king came down to him.
It happened according to word of man of Divine to king, saying, Two seahs of barley for one shekel and a seah of fine flour for one shekel shall be about this time tomorrow at gate of Samaria.

The officer answered man of Divine and said, Look, if YHWH made windows in heavens, could it be according to this word? He said, Look, you shall see it with your eyes, but from there you shall not eat.
So it happened to him: people trampled him in gate, and he died.

translation_notes: The four men at the gate are excluded from the besieged city because of skin disease. Their marginalization places them between starvation inside and enemy danger outside.
The term traditionally translated lepers does not securely identify Hansen's disease. Avoid contagion mythology and disability stigma.
Their decision is not reckless heroism but survival calculation under conditions where every available option may end in death.
The excluded men first eat, drink, and secure goods. Starving people meeting abundance should not be judged for immediate survival behavior.
They then recognize a duty to share good news. The people ignored by the city become the city's life-saving messengers.
The king's suspicion is rational after siege deception; verification before mass movement is prudent rather than faithlessness.
The abandoned Aramean camp becomes famine relief through plunder. This does not romanticize war economies or justify looting outside the narrative.
The officer dies by crowd trampling at the gate. His skepticism does not make crowd-crush death an acceptable punishment or prove doubters deserve harm.
Rapid food-price reversal is a narrative miracle, not an economic promise that faith guarantees cheap food or sudden market recovery.
safety_note: Do not stigmatize skin disease, excluded people, hunger behavior, or skepticism. Do not celebrate crowd-crush death or use it to threaten doubters. Center the four marginalized men as survival witnesses whose disclosure saves a city, and treat safe verification and equitable food access as essential.
